payload.text: THE DISPATCHER IGNORES AN INHERITED UTILZ_HOME AND ALWAYS DERIVES ITS TREE FROM $0. RE-RULED by hv 8 Sep, reversing vc's ruling of the previous evening, and hv is right. bin/utilz:42 derived from $0 only when the variable was unset, so an exported value silently redirected an install at the checkout. vc's first ruling kept the honouring and added an stderr announcement, on a measurement that UTILZ_HOME is load-bearing in five places. THAT MEASUREMENT WAS ABOUT THE LIBRARY AND WAS APPLIED TO THE DISPATCHER, WHICH IS THE CONFLATION hv CAUGHT. Re-measured 8 Sep, every consumer sorted by what it actually invokes: test_helper.bash:20 sets it to the tree $0 already lives in (convergent, derive gives the identical answer); common_lib.bats:71 and install.sh:124 source the LIBRARY and never run the dispatcher; opt/prez/prez:24 carries its own ${UTILZ_HOME:-derive} and receives the dispatcher's exported value anyway; cleanz.bats:575 and install_guards.bats:107,120,191,207 are all convergent. THE ONLY DIVERGENT DISPATCHER INVOCATIONS IN THE ENTIRE TREE ARE install_guards.bats:166 AND :217, WHICH ARE THE TESTS OF THE ANNOUNCEMENT ITSELF. A behaviour whose only consumer is its own test is circular, and removing it removes the test rather than breaking anything. So the class is DELETED rather than reported: with no divergence possible there is nothing to announce, AC17's refusal clause has nothing to refuse, and a user with the variable set simply gets the tree they invoked. The library keeps reading $UTILZ_HOME and the dispatcher keeps EXPORTING the derived value, so children resolve correctly; what goes is the dispatcher treating an inherited value as authoritative over its own location.
